key: Unto Allah belong the East and the West, and whithersoever ye turn, there is Allah’s Countenance.
s: Following a warning against barring worshippers from Allah’s sanctuaries, the surah claims every direction for Him; al-Tabari, on 2:115, reads the naming of East and West as teaching believers that all creatures between them are His and owe Him obedience, facing wherever He directs them.

evidence.words: والصواب من القول في ذلك: أن الله تعالى ذكره إنما خص الخبر عن المشرق والمغرب في هذه الآية بأنهما له ملكا، وإن كان لا شيء إلا وهو له ملك - إعلاما منه عباده المؤمنين أن له ملكهما وملك ما بينهما من الخلق، وأن على جميعهم = إذ كان له ملكهم = طاعته فيما أمرهم ونهاهم، وفيما فرض عليهم من الفرائض، والتوجهِ نحو الوجه الذي وجهوا إليه، إذْ كان من حكم المماليك طاعة مالكهم
evidence.gloss: The right view is that God singled out East and West in this ayah as His possession, though nothing is not His, to inform His believing servants that He owns them both and the creatures between them, and that all of these, being His, owe Him obedience in what He commands and forbids, in the duties He lays on them, and in turning toward the direction to which they are turned, since those owned must obey their owner.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Al-Baqarah 2:115, at 121). Plain sense faithful: 2:114 condemns whoever forbids the approach to the sanctuaries of Allah and 2:115 follows; no four-word run from the verse. In the packet on 2:115 al-Tabari first reports the views on why East and West are named (the Jews’ qibla, travel and prayer, the change of qibla, and others), then gives his own sound view: the two are named to teach believers that He owns them and all creatures between them, who therefore owe Him obedience, including in turning to the direction He sets. The sentence carries exactly this; it does not import his separate discussion of abrogation or of wajh. Evidence cut by script from the packet text. Entry-check ok.
